_comment: California Curated Trivia question pool. Hand-written seed batch — once this lives, a weekly GitHub Action will draft new questions from articles via Claude Haiku and stage them in /drafts/ for review. Each question is referenced by id in localStorage so we can avoid recycling questions a player has already seen.

questions.question: California's grizzly bear, still pictured on the state flag, went extinct in the wild around what year?
questions.explanation: The last confirmed California grizzly was shot in 1922, and the species was declared extinct by 1924. It now exists only on the flag.

questions.question: The bastnaesite ore at California's Mountain Pass mine contains rare earth elements at roughly what concentration?
questions.explanation: Mountain Pass ore averages 7 to 8 percent rare earths, among the richest concentrations anywhere on Earth.

source.title: The Mountain Pass Mine in California

questions.question: The oldest known non-clonal living organisms on Earth are bristlecone pines in California's White Mountains. How old is the oldest?
questions.explanation: Methuselah, in the Ancient Bristlecone Pine Forest, is roughly 4,800 years old. A still-older bristlecone has been measured at over 5,000 years.

source.title: The Majesty and Mystery of California's Bristlecone Pine

questions.question: When the California condor recovery program began in the 1980s, how many condors remained in the wild?
questions.explanation: Just 22 condors remained when biologists captured them all for a captive breeding program. The 1,000th chick hatched in 2019.

questions.question: California's state marine fish is the:
questions.explanation: The bright-orange Garibaldi, a damselfish that lives among California's kelp forests, became the official state marine fish in 1995.

questions.question: Lake Tulare, once the largest freshwater lake west of the Mississippi, was drained primarily for what purpose?
questions.explanation: Tulare Lake was systematically diverted and drained beginning in the late 1800s to convert its bed into farmland for cotton, alfalfa, and tomatoes.

questions.question: Monterey Canyon, off California's central coast, is comparable in scale to which famous landmark?
questions.explanation: Monterey Canyon is roughly 95 miles long and a mile deep at its deepest point, comparable to the Grand Canyon in size and steepness.

source.title: A Deep Dive into Monterey Canyon

questions.question: California's tallest peak, Mount Whitney, rises to what elevation?
questions.explanation: Mount Whitney's summit is officially 14,505 feet, making it the highest peak in the contiguous United States.

questions.question: Badwater Basin in California's Death Valley is the lowest point in North America. How far below sea level?
questions.explanation: Badwater Basin sits 282 feet (86 meters) below sea level. Mount Whitney, the highest point in the lower 48, is only 85 miles away.

questions.question: Joshua trees, found across California's Mojave Desert, are actually giant members of which plant family?
questions.explanation: Joshua trees (Yucca brevifolia) are not trees at all but giant yuccas in the agave family — closer to asparagus than to oak.

source.title: The Mystical Sentinels of the Mojave

questions.question: California sea otters are essential to kelp forests because they prey primarily on:
questions.explanation: Otters eat sea urchins, which graze on kelp. Without otters, urchin populations explode and clear-cut entire kelp forests in what's called an 'urchin barren.'

source.title: Why Bringing Back California's Kelp Is So Important

questions.question: The Long Valley Caldera near Mammoth Lakes is a:
questions.explanation: Long Valley Caldera formed in a colossal eruption 760,000 years ago. It's one of the largest supervolcanic calderas in the world and remains geologically active.

questions.question: J. Robert Oppenheimer launched his academic career at which California institution before leading the Manhattan Project?
questions.explanation: Oppenheimer joined UC Berkeley in 1929 and built a world-leading theoretical physics group there before being recruited to Los Alamos.

questions.question: The 'Alvarez hypothesis' — that an asteroid impact killed the dinosaurs — was proposed by UC Berkeley researchers in what year?
questions.explanation: Luis Alvarez and his son Walter published their iridium-layer evidence in Science in 1980. The Chicxulub crater confirmed the theory a decade later.

questions.question: Albert Einstein spent three winters during the early 1930s as a visiting researcher at which California institution?
questions.explanation: Einstein wintered at Caltech in Pasadena from 1931 to 1933, where he worked alongside Edwin Hubble and confronted the new evidence of an expanding universe.

source.title: Einstein in Pasadena: Three Winters in Paradise

questions.question: California's state fossil is the:
questions.explanation: Smilodon fatalis, the saber-toothed cat, became the official state fossil in 1973, in part because thousands of specimens have been recovered from the La Brea Tar Pits.

questions.question: The Channel Islands' island fox is unusual primarily because it is:
choices: The smallest fox in North America
questions.explanation: Island foxes are roughly the size of a house cat — the smallest fox species in North America. They evolved in isolation on the Channel Islands for ~10,000 years.

questions.question: Hydraulic mining during the Gold Rush was banned in 1884 primarily because:
choices: It caused catastrophic flooding and farmland destruction
Workers refused to do the dangerous work
The federal government seized the land
questions.explanation: The 1884 Sawyer Decision halted hydraulic mining after sediment-choked rivers triggered devastating floods in Sacramento Valley farmland. It's considered America's first major environmental ruling.

questions.question: California produces approximately what share of the world's almonds?
questions.explanation: California grows roughly 80 percent of the world's almonds, almost all of them in the Central Valley.

questions.question: Caltech's NASA-affiliated facility in Pasadena, which built and operates the Mars rovers, is known as:
questions.explanation: The Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) is managed by Caltech for NASA. JPL has led every U.S. Mars rover mission, from Sojourner in 1997 through Perseverance.

questions.question: A single modern wind turbine can require up to how many pounds of rare-earth metals?
questions.explanation: The high-strength permanent magnets in a single turbine can use up to 500 pounds of neodymium and dysprosium — a major reason California's Mountain Pass mine is strategically important.

source.title: The Mountain Pass Mine in California

questions.question: The California Current, which runs along the coast, is:
questions.explanation: The California Current is a cold, south-flowing current that drives the upwelling responsible for California's rich coastal fisheries and famously chilly summer ocean.

questions.question: The Pentagon recently became the largest single shareholder in California rare-earth miner MP Materials, with an equity stake of roughly:
questions.explanation: In July 2025 the U.S. Department of Defense invested $400 million in MP Materials in exchange for convertible preferred stock and warrants, making it the company's largest shareholder at about 15 percent.

source.title: The Mountain Pass Mine in California

questions.question: The 1872 Lone Pine earthquake in California's Owens Valley is estimated to have been:
questions.explanation: The Lone Pine quake was approximately magnitude 7.9, killing 27 people and offsetting the Sierra Nevada by as much as 20 feet vertically.

questions.question: Coast redwoods, the tallest trees on Earth, can grow taller than:
questions.explanation: Hyperion, in Redwood National Park, has been measured at over 380 feet — taller than the Statue of Liberty including its pedestal.
